verdict.rationale: Natural language is central to NotebookLM's core interaction: users chat with their notebook and ask questions grounded in sources (notebooklm-docs-2, notebooklm-docs-28), set custom response styles or roles in plain-language prompts (notebooklm-docs-7), and define custom report types (notebooklm-docs-27). However, the documented way to run product actions (generating audio, video, slides or mind maps, managing sources, exporting) is through UI selections, so natural language mainly drives Q&A and customization rather than operating the product. Missing for 10: evidence that natural-language commands can trigger product actions (artifact generation, source management, sharing/export), and an agentic command interface beyond chat Q&A.
